summary: The clearest law-violence divergence in the country: Trans Health Equity Act and refuge/shield protections (Most Protective tier), and the second-highest killing rate (11.1 per 100k trans women/yr), including two Black trans women shot dead in Baltimore ten weeks apart in 2026. Protective law does not by itself make people safer. Above the national score 0.36, capped by the violence data.

sources.summary: Data-driven essay (July 2026) arguing legal-risk tiers do not predict physical safety for trans women: overlaying Trans Murder Monitoring records (428 confirmed US killings 2008-2025, explicitly a floor) on the legislative risk map, Maryland sits in the 'most protective' legal group yet records 11.1 killings per 100k trans women per year — the second-highest state rate in the country, behind only Louisiana's 11.6; 90% of US victims were trans women or transfeminine.

Regional LGBTQ+ news blog (13 September 2026): two Black trans women were shot dead in Baltimore ten weeks apart, the most recent being Sophie Lee, 27, found dying of multiple gunshot wounds in the Charles Village neighbourhood on Friday 11 September 2026, with the suspect at large; the piece situates the killings within an undercounted wave of fatal violence against Black trans women.

Legal blog post on Maryland's Trans Health Equity Act (House Bill 283, passed the House 93-37, effective 1 January 2024): mandates Medicaid coverage of gender-affirming treatment - hormones, puberty blockers and surgery - for an estimated 94,000 transgender and nonbinary state residents, making care access one of the most protective legal layers in the country.

localsOnly: The Trans Health Equity Act's Medicaid expansion covers gender-affirming treatment for the state's estimated 94,000 trans and nonbinary residents - a care-access benefit a short-term visitor does not draw on.
